title: InjuryAlerTNFL — Sideline Signal: source-checked NFL in-game injury board
description: Mobile-friendly NFL scoreboard and in-game injury-alert prototype that keeps three things apart: what was observed, what happened in that game, and later-reported availability. The published archive holds 80 manually source-checked 2026 in-game incidents (data/archive.json → incidents, counted at head 6a4067a) carrying 154 dated claims between them, each with a short excerpt and a link to NFL.com or an official club page; 21 separately flagged source disagreements sit in data/review.json → flags. A GitHub Actions collector reads NFL.com's public roundup index and recent in-game roundups and a deliberately conservative parser republishes only explicit single-player return/out phrases — never a group claim, never an inference from silence, and never an LLM-written prognosis. Its suites were executed in a clean clone: python -m unittest discover -s tests → 18 tests OK, node --test tests/ui.test.mjs → 6 pass / 0 fail.
lastUpdatedField: lastCommit (newest committer timestamp on the default branch; the public API exposes no site-visit or last-use date)
flags: The README states that scheduled runs “have never fired” and that the */5 cron “produced zero schedule events up to September 23, 2026”. The Actions API records exactly one schedule event on the publish workflow, created 2026-09-23T23:07:03Z — 44 minutes before that README's own head commit 6a4067a at 23:51:01Z — and the run concluded cancelled. The “zero schedule events” claim is therefore false at head; the README's operational warning (a five-minute cron is not a five-minute delivery guarantee) still stands (IRR-106).
Not a complete injury census and not a live medical record: 80 selected Week 1–2 incidents. The site documents that an empty incident list means “not checked”, not “nobody was injured”.
Scores come from a public, unsupported ESPN endpoint with no contractual availability guarantee, so game matching stops whenever scores cannot be verified — the README's own recorded limitation.

GitHub reports a legacy main/root Pages source for this repository while its workflow deploys a generated artifact, and the README records that a legacy build once overwrote a good artifact deployment. It also states the integration cannot change the Pages build setting via API (403), so an administrator must set the source to GitHub Actions to remove the workaround.

Requires a GitHub Action to keep its five-minute feed fresh; up to 2026-09-24T00:05Z only one scheduled run had ever been created, and it was cancelled, so every refresh so far has come from a main-branch push.
verifiedBasis: New entry this pass, read in full at head 6a4067a (2026-09-23T23:51:01Z) from a shallow clone. Executed in that clone: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v → Ran 18 tests, OK; node --test tests/ui.test.mjs → tests 6, pass 6, fail 0. Counted with json.load rather than quoted: data/archive.json → incidents 80, verifiedOn 2026-09-23; the 80 incidents together hold 154 claim objects; data/review.json → flags 21. The README's arithmetic was reconciled rather than trusted: its 'first 123 quotes re-fetched' plus '31 excerpts added after' equals the 154 claims counted in the archive, so the two figures are consistent with the file. The schedule-event claim was checked independently against GET https://api.github.com/repos/buffedlizard55-lab/InjuryAlerTNFL/actions/runs, which returns 54 runs: 24 push, 19 pull_request, 10 dynamic and 1 schedule (created 2026-09-23T23:07:03Z, conclusion cancelled) — see IRR-106.
